newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says EU studying Albania initiative.
newsitem.headline: France says EU studying Albania initiative.

text.p: France, voicing "extreme concern" at worsening unrest in Albania, said on Thursday the European Union was discussing how it could help end the crisis through dialogue between the government and the opposition.
"We are extremely concerned by the situation in Albania," said a French Foreign Ministry statement.

"We are in close touch with our European Union partners to study the details of an EU initiative to promote dialogue between the government and the opposition and help solve the current crisis," it said.

Albania, Europe's poorhouse, has been rocked by a month of anti-government protests after a series of dubious get-rich-quick investment schemes collapsed, robbing hundreds of thousands of their life savings.
Clashes in the Adriatic port of Vlore were among the worst unrest Albania has seen since communism was toppled in 1990.

Irate investors, demanding the resignation of President Sali Berisha, accuse him of letting the funds flourish. Opposition parties said his Democratic Party used money from the schemes to finance a winning election campaign last year.
The government has denied the allegations and is trying to contain the damage by offering some investors partial refunds.

International criticism has been mounting over Berisha's handling of the crisis. The Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) has said it was deeply worried about the violence. Britain has expressed concern about reports of arrests and intimidation of opposition leaders.
Italy advised its nationals on Thursday to consider restricting travel within and to Albania to essential business over the next few days.
About 400 Italians live in Albania, a short distance across the Adriatic from Italy.
